clickhouse.licences: LGPL (libgsasl, libssh, mariadb-connector-c, numactl, xz, lemmagen-c), GPL-2.0-or-BSD (ittapi), MPL-2.0; ClickHouse itself is Apache-2.0

verification.method: docker image inspect of the digest-qualified reference: the image Id (containerd store) or a RepoDigests entry equals digest; nothing is pulled

clickhouse.why: Static LGPL libraries in the server binary. Held out of the kit pending the user's licence review (question 247): the builder refuses to declare it, so the kit never needs it and the list reports it outside the kit

debian-bookworm-slim-base-image.licences: GPL (e.g. bash, coreutils, tar, sed, findutils, login), LGPL (libc6, libgnutls30, libgmp10)

verification.method: docker image inspect of the digest-qualified reference: the image Id (containerd store) or a RepoDigests entry equals digest; nothing is pulled

debian-bookworm-slim-base-image.why: OS userland in the image's base layers; the kit carries only the application layer and a Dockerfile that starts FROM this digest

linux-aarch64.reason: NASA's GMAT R2026a folder on SourceForge (https://sourceforge.net/projects/gmat/files/GMAT/GMAT-R2026a/, read 2026-10-18) lists no Linux aarch64 build: its Linux archives are gmat-ubuntu-x64-R2026a.tar.gz and gmat-rhel7-x64-R2026a.tar.gz, both x86_64. The key stays null until NASA publishes one (question 254, task 12)

linux-x86_64.final_url_note: SourceForge's mirror answers with a per-request query (viasf, fid, e, st); it is omitted here because it expires

linux-x86_64-rhel7-measured-not-pinned.note: the second Linux archive NASA publishes, a different tree from the Ubuntu one; a platform key holds one pin, and SourceForge's own default Linux download is the Ubuntu archive, so this one is recorded and not pinned

gmat-r2026a.how_to_add_a_pin: see scripts/kit/README.md, 'GMAT is operator-supplied': measure the unpacked release with manifest.measure_tree(root, scope) on the target platform and replace that platform's null with the five fields
gmat-r2026a.licences: OSGPL (LGPL-2.1 with extra permissions: libosg*, libOpenThreads, osgdb_* plugins), wxWindows Library Licence (LGPL-2.0+ with a binary exception: libwx_*); GMAT itself is Apache-2.0
not_covered: file modes, ownership, timestamps, extended attributes and empty directories: the content hash covers the relative path and bytes of each regular file, the symlink listing covers each link's path and target

everything the scope leaves out: files the operator's own use of the tree writes (output/, __pycache__ bytecode, bin/api_startup_file.txt, which api/BuildApiStartupFile.py generates and which holds the install's absolute path)
anything that changes after the install-time check
gmat-r2026a.reference: GMAT R2026a, NASA's release for the target platform (SourceForge), unpacked

verification.method: manifest.measure_tree over the operator's unpacked tree under the pin's scope, compared with the pin for the named platform (content hash, file count, total bytes, symlink count, symlink listing hash)

gmat-r2026a.why: GMAT R2026a bundles OpenSceneGraph and wxWidgets (LGPL); the kit records GMAT's pack descriptor and never carries its bytes (docs/kit-operator-supplied.md item 3). The installer measures the operator's unpacked release and compares it with the pin for the target platform

numpy-wheel-linux-aarch64.licences: libgfortran (numpy.libs/libgfortran-e1b7dfc8-d8198c01.so.5.0.0) is GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1; the wheel also bundles OpenBLAS (numpy.libs/libscipy_openblas64_-f552eb69.so), BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause-Open-MPI, and numpy itself is BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0
numpy-wheel-linux-aarch64.reference: PyPI, numpy 2.5.3, file numpy-2.5.3-cp313-cp313-manylinux_2_27_aarch64.manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl (https://pypi.org/project/numpy/2.5.3/#files); scripts/kit/save_operator_wheels.py downloads exactly this file

verification.method: sha256 of <operator-wheels DIR>/<filename> equals sha256; the verified file is copied under the target and pip installs the copy by path

numpy-wheel-linux-aarch64.why: The kit redistributes no GPL or LGPL code. numpy's linux/aarch64 wheel bundles libgfortran, GPL-3.0 code under the GCC Runtime Library Exception; the exception frees numpy as a combined work, not the library file. So the kit does not carry this wheel (KIT_MANIFEST wheels.operator_supplied) and the installer requires the operator's copy (--operator-wheels)

postgis.licences: PostGIS is GPL-2.0-or-later (PostgreSQL itself is the permissive PostgreSQL licence), run unmodified over the Postgres wire protocol

verification.method: docker image inspect of the digest-qualified reference: the image Id (containerd store) or a RepoDigests entry equals digest; nothing is pulled

postgis.why: Network service (the catalog's PostgreSQL + PostGIS); outside the kit unless a site that deploys it builds the kit with --declare-operator-supplied postgis

versitygw.licences: Versity Gateway is Apache-2.0; the image's Alpine 3.24.2 base layers are GPL-2.0-only (busybox, busybox-binsh, ssl_client, apk-tools, libapk, alpine-baselayout, alpine-baselayout-data, scanelf), MIT AND BSD-2-Clause AND GPL-2.0-or-later (musl-utils), MPL-2.0 AND MIT (ca-certificates-bundle), and MIT, Apache-2.0 or Zlib for the rest (alpine-keys, alpine-release, musl, libcrypto3, libssl3, zlib)

versitygw.why: Network service (the heavy track's object store). Operator-supplied because the upstream image's Alpine base layers carry GPL-2.0-only packages and the kit redistributes no GPL or LGPL code (question 251); outside the kit unless a site that deploys the object store builds the kit with --declare-operator-supplied versitygw.
